data.name: Keyansh
data.gender_notes: Keyansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Keyansh is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Kay' meaning God and 'Ansh' meaning treasure. This name signifies that the bearer of this name is a God's treasure. In Hindu mythology, Lord Vishnu is often depicted as having a treasure (Ansh) of the universe in his navel. The name Keyansh carries the meaning “God's treasure” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Keyansh usually hope their child will grow to embody god's treasure and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Keyansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's treasure.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Keyansh total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Keyansh is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. He was a Yadava prince, the son of Krishna's cousin Shatanik and Krishna's friend Ugrasena. Keyansh was a powerful warrior and a devotee of Lord Krishna. He played a significant role in the Kurukshetra War.

Another reference to Keyansh can be found in the Puranas, a set of sacred texts in Hinduism. According to these texts, Keyansh was the name of a king who ruled in the city of Mathura during the Dwapara Yuga. He was a great devotee of Lord Vishnu and is said to have performed many penances to seek the divine blessings.
